justification.statement: Gaussian elimination over a prime field keeps the row space and the solution set
justification.text: Swapping rows, scaling a row by a nonzero element and subtracting a multiple of one row from another keep the row space and the solution set; in echelon form the rank is the number of pivots and the system is solvable when no row reads 0 = c with c nonzero.

reason.statement: Gaussian elimination over a prime field keeps the row space and the solution set
reason.idea: Elimination keeps what the rows span and what solves the equations while making the matrix triangular; the rank is the number of pivots.

failure.hypothesis: the modulus is a prime, so every nonzero element has an inverse
failure.outcome: counterexample modulo 4, which is not a field: 2·x = 1 has no solution although 2 is nonzero, so elimination's division step fails

by_hand.not_meant: A rank or a solution over F2 or F5 asserts nothing about which states twists reach (the catalogue row's note); the correction library's rows are research data.

steps.check: Over F5 the matrix is diagonal with entries 4 and 1, both nonzero.
A diagonal matrix with nonzero diagonal entries has one pivot per row: rank 2.
Rank 2 on 2 unknowns: every right-hand side has a solution.

leaf_specs.none: the decomposition reaches no kernel leaf: the module is pure (LG3.2), so every part of it is a base part of the IR
